title: check_tfs: find entries that define value_string identical to common tfs
description:
The idea is to check for places where value_string has been used, and (in terms of values and strings) is identical to a 'common' true_value_string pair defined in epan/tfs.c

There are some differences between them, however:
- TFS() must be used with fields that are FT_BOOLEAN, whereas VALS() would be with an integer type of some sort (not necessary with a bitmask). With FT_BOOLEAN, a bitmask does not need to be supplied - in this case the active bit will still be the l.s.b., and the output should look the same
- There may be some protocols defined to have > 1 bits (e.g. a whole number of bytes) devoted to a field, but only 2 values, and showing as a boolean field may not seem right.  Possibly the enum could grow in the future, but if it matches a pairs in tfs.c, they are most likely opposites meanings, other choices seem unlikely.

Not (yet) included in pipeline.

+class ValueString:
+    def __init__(self, file, name, vals):
+        self.file = file
+        self.name = name
+        self.raw_vals = vals
+        self.parsed_vals = {}
+        self.looks_like_tfs = True
+
+        no_lines =  self.raw_vals.count('{')
+        if no_lines != 3:
+            self.looks_like_tfs = False
+            return
+
+        # Now parse out each entry in the value_string
+        matches = re.finditer(r'\{([\"a-zA-Z\s\d\,]*)\}', self.raw_vals)
+        for m in matches:
+            entry = m[1]
+            # Check each entry looks like part of a TFS entry.
+            match = re.match(r'\s*([01])\,\s*\"([a-zA-Z\d\s]*\s*)\"', entry)
+            if match:
+                if match[1] == '1':
+                    self.parsed_vals[True] = match[2]
+                else:
+                    self.parsed_vals[False] = match[2]
+
+                # Now have both entries
+                if len(self.parsed_vals) == 2:
+                    break
+            else:
+                self.looks_like_tfs = False
+                break
+
+    def __str__(self):
+        return '{' + '"' + self.raw_vals + '"}'
+
